### **Course List:**

**Fundamental Bioinformatics courses** (recommended for 1st and 2nd year undergraduate students)

* ### **C1 | Fundamental Bioinformatics: Databases & Data Mining**

* ### **C2 | Fundamental Bioinformatics: Sequence Analysis, Functional Annotation & Phylogeny**

**Domain Specialized courses** (Recommended for 2nd year/upper class)

Unlock the Secrets of Life with Specialized Training\!

Harnessing Data: With advanced NGS technology, we can analyze genomes at unprecedented scales. Training in NGS data analysis equips students to interpret complex genomic information, vital for understanding gene regulation and expression patterns related to health and disease.

The Power of Proteomics: While DNA is the blueprint of life, proteins are the executors. Specialized courses in computational proteomics enable students to analyze proteome-level data, providing insights into cellular processes crucial for drug development and therapeutic interventions.

Innovative Drug Design: Cheminformatics integrates chemistry with computational tools, streamlining drug discovery. This training empowers students to identify new drug targets and develop effective therapeutics, preparing them for high-demand careers in pharmaceuticals.

By bridging these disciplines, students position themselves at the forefront of scientific innovation. Join us in exploring the depths of biological information and contribute to groundbreaking discoveries for a healthier future\!

* ### **C5 | Computational Proteomics and Systems Biology**

* ### **C10 | Cheminformatics: Drug Target Discovery and Computer-aided Drug Design**

* ### **C14 | NGS data analysis: ChIP-seq, RNA-seq & eQTLs**

* **C17 | Data Science and Machine Learning for Biologists**

**Programming Language Courses** (Recommended for 2nd year/ upper class undergrad students)

Master the Tools of Modern Science with R, Python, and UNIX/Linux\!

In today’s data-driven world, proficiency in R, Python, and UNIX/Linux command line is essential for tackling complex scientific challenges and making data meaningful.

**Why R?** R is a powerhouse for statistical analysis and data visualization, enabling researchers to interpret and communicate insights with clarity. In any research field, R’s specialized libraries make it an invaluable tool for handling and visualizing data effectively.

**Why Python?** Known for its versatility, Python is widely used in scientific computing, machine learning, deep learning, data analysis and AI. Its simplicity and robust libraries allow scientists to process large datasets, automate tasks, and build sophisticated models, making it ideal for everything from genomics to drug discovery.

**Why UNIX/Linux Command Line?** For managing, processing, and analyzing vast amounts of data, Windows isn’t useful. Also, many advanced bioinformatics tools are available as Linux command line tools only. The UNIX/Linux command line interface enables researchers to handle high-throughput data, automate workflows, and work efficiently on large-scale projects.

These tools not only give students hands-on technical expertise but also prepare them to tackle real-world problems in research and industry. Join us to master the essential skills that power today’s scientific breakthroughs\!

* ### **C6 | Introduction to UNIX and Linux**

* ### **C8 | Python/Biopython for Bioinformatics**

* ### [**C9 | Basic Statistics & R for Bioinformatic**](https://www.cblast.du.ac.bd/course/view.php?id=24)**s**

**How to Enroll:** 

If you want to register, 

1. Please go to our website [www.cblast.du.ac.bd](http://www.cblast.du.ac.bd) and check out the "Enrollment requirements" segment to learn the details of how to make payment.   
2. Then fill up the form from "register/re-enroll a course" to register to the course of your liking.  
3. Finally create an account on our website so that we can give you access to your course material to your account.  
4. Wait for 24 hours before you get access to your course. You do not need to inform us after creating your account, we will be notified by the system.
